content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Platform Engineering | QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer focused on CI/CD, test infrastructure and build tooling, with hands-on experience supporting three product teams. Built GitLab CI pipelines and Helm-based ephemeral environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster, and improved pipeline speed and test reliability through automation and measurement. Developing infrastructure-as-code and cloud skills through a personal k3s/GitOps homelab and Terraform work on Hetzner. Known for documenting technical workflows and helping teams adopt shared tooling.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and Infrastructure: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access; test environments), Terraform (personal project), Argo CD
Monitoring and Data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Programming and Automation: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, Ansible (basic)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems: Linux, Git
Cloud learning: AWS fundamentals (EC2, S3); personal Hetzner VPS

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by approximately 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Developed Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding.
- Created an internal guide to the CI system used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, plus Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Delivered an automated workflow deploying a short-lived application, PostgreSQL and seeded-data environment for each merge request via GitLab CI and Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Configured automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity; QA and product teams use the environments for feature review, with end-to-end tests running against them.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and separated end-to-end testing into its own stage.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by approximately 30%.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards to show flaky tests by team.
- Helped teams identify recurring test issues; the flaky-test rate fell from 7% to below 1%.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam scheduled for January 2027 (not yet certified)

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible CV with a clear progression from QA automation into DevOps and platform engineering. It uses quantified outcomes effectively, including the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, approximately 30% lower runner costs, and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The professional summary is targeted and appropriately transparent about personal-project and access-level experience. The main content weakness is some duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Infrastructure Projects; the CV could be slightly more concise and make the candidate's technical leadership and stakeholder impact more explicit using evidence already present.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings, simple text formatting, conventional reverse-chronological experience, and recognizable technology names such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, AWS, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, and PostgreSQL. It should parse well and has a good AI-screening probability for QA automation, CI/CD, test infrastructure, and junior-to-mid DevOps/platform roles. Screening probability for this specific cloud infrastructure contractor role is moderate rather than high because the document does not show Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, network design, production cloud operations, or a strong AWS track record; these are genuine experience gaps rather than keyword problems. The CV correctly avoids claiming CKA certification and accurately labels Terraform, AWS, and Kubernetes scope.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows relevant hands-on infrastructure work through GitLab CI ownership, Helm-based ephemeral environments, namespace-level Kubernetes work, Docker, monitoring, Terraform on Hetzner, and a k3s/GitOps homelab. It also demonstrates analytical thinking and communication through pipeline profiling, measurable optimization, technical documentation, onboarding support, and mentoring. AWS fundamentals are present, but only through learning/personal work. The largest gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt, system architecture and system design, networking including mTLS, practical security experience beyond TLS certificate tooling, production cloud operation, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack experience. The CV is a credible adjacent match, but not yet a strong match for a contractor expected to shape train-to-cloud architecture and lead the infrastructure into production. Its evidence of ownership, shared tooling, documentation, and cross-team enablement aligns with Corvale's collaborative, engineering-led culture.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary section, make the strongest infrastructure evidence more concrete by replacing "Developing infrastructure-as-code and cloud skills through a personal k3s/GitOps homelab and Terraform work on Hetzner" with: "Built a personal three-node k3s/GitOps homelab with Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, and provisioned a Hetzner VPS with Terraform; also have AWS fundamentals covering EC2 and S3." This improves ATS keyword visibility while preserving the personal-project scope.
2. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, make the stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence more explicit without overstating formal leadership. Change the final bullet to: "Created the internal CI-system guide used in team onboarding, helping three product teams adopt shared pipeline and test-environment workflows; mentored two QA interns in 2023." This is supported by the existing CV and better addresses the requirement to lead technical topics and bring stakeholders along.
3. In Selected Infrastructure Projects under "Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments," clarify the Kubernetes scope by changing "deployed via Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster" to "deployed via Helm to namespaces on the company's shared Kubernetes cluster." This preserves the achievement while matching the candidate's stated namespace-level access and avoiding any implication of cluster administration.
4. To reduce repetition, retain the detailed technical bullets in Selected Infrastructure Projects but shorten the corresponding repeated bullets in Professional Experience. For example, under Odrava Health Software, keep the quantified pipeline result and ownership bullet, but remove or consolidate details repeated verbatim in the "CI Pipeline Speed-up" and "Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments" project entries. This will make the CV more concise without removing evidence.
5. In the Technical Skills section, change "Terraform (personal project)" to "Terraform (Hetzner VPS, personal project)" and change "Cloud learning: AWS fundamentals (EC2, S3); personal Hetzner VPS" to "Cloud: AWS fundamentals (EC2, S3, learning); Hetzner VPS (personal project)." This gives recruiters clearer context about the depth and source of the experience.
